bugs.what: Script 7 creates boolean cutter object 'hole' (25 cylinders spanning z = 0.5..0.7 m at (13.5, 3.3)) and links it to the scene collection before modifier_apply fails with RuntimeError on multi-user mesh data, skipping removal. Script 8 creates a second cutter ('hole.001') and only deletes that new object, leaving 'hole' protruding above the raised floor in Cold Aisle 1 in the final scene.

Wrong local Z maths on bmesh.ops.create_cube(bm, size=1.0): vertices already span [-0.5, 0.5], so scaling z by thickness and also subtracting half-thickness shifted local Z to [-thickness, 0] instead of [-thickness/2, +thickness/2]. Combined with location.z = 0.6 - thickness/2, tile top faces sat at z = 0.58 m (script 2) and z = 0.585 m (scripts 5-6) instead of 0.6 m until corrected in script 8.

Boolean cutter cylinders were built around world origin (0, 0, 0) while master tile PerfTile_1_01 was already placed at (13.5, 3.3, 0.585), so the DIFFERENCE boolean missed the tile completely (cutting zero holes) and reassigned only one tile's mesh datablock instead of all 34.
dup_tree called new.children.clear(), raising AttributeError because bpy Object.children is a read-only tuple (and Object.copy() does not duplicate children).
overlap(a[1:], b[1:]) passed 4-element slices (x0, x1, y0, y1) to overlap(), which indexed a[0], a[2], a[3], a[4], mixing slice indices with 5-tuple indices and raising IndexError in script 2.

verify.py checked rack corners in metres against data['room']['polygon'] in millimetres, and unpacked corners as ((rb[1], rb[2]), (rb[1], rb[3]), (rb[2], rb[2]), (rb[2], rb[3])), using x1 (rb[2]) as a Y coordinate and omitting y1 (rb[4]).

Tile naming PerfTile_{a_idx}_{n+1:02d} used a global tile index n alongside per-aisle index a_idx without resetting n per aisle, leading to KeyError on 'PerfTile_3_10' in script 6; script 7 then attempted modifier_apply on 34-user mesh data without making a single-user copy first.

strengths: Accurately derives all rack positions, template choices (RackG vs RackA), compass rotations (-y unrotated mapped cleanly to N/S/E/W), cold-aisle roofs and end doors, 600 mm floor-tile grid cells, and row cable trays from layout.json.

Good scene memory economy: uses recursive linked duplicates preserving matrix_parent_inverse for all 58 rack hierarchies and shares a single perforated mesh datablock across all 34 PerfTile_* objects.
Evaluated depsgraph world-bounding-box checks in scripts 6 and 8 caught the tile Z-offset error and verified both top-face alignment at z = 0.6 m and the 310-face perforated mesh topology.
X.summary: All required racks, containment parts, perforated floor tiles, and cable trays end up accurately positioned, oriented, named, and instanced from layout.json, with rackId custom properties intact. However, the workflow took 9 scripts with 4 runtime failures due to careless tuple indexing, bpy API mistakes, and repeated Z-offset/boolean errors while reworking the floor tiles, ultimately leaving an uncleaned boolean cutter object ('hole') visible in Cold Aisle 1 because final verification only counted expected name prefixes rather than auditing all scene objects or checking actual scene wall/column geometry.

bugs.where: script 1 (build.py, line 74), patched in memory by script 3 (fix.py, line 1398ff.)
bugs.what: Setting root.scale = (1, 1, 1) overwrote the RackG template root scale of (1.3333, 1.0, 1.0), shrinking the three 800 mm GPU racks (B01, B02, B03) to 600 mm wide; caught by the script's own world bounding-box verification and patched in the live session via exec/replace in script 3, though build.py on disk remained unedited.

bugs.where: script 1 (build.py, lines 45-56-ish in dup_tree, right before copy_rack)
bugs.what: Unused, unfinished helper function dup_tree containing dead 'if False else None' expressions was left in the script instead of being removed.

bugs.where: script 1 (build.py, inside the rack verification loop)
bugs.what: Unused result: fwd = root.matrix_world.to_3x3() @ Vector((0, -1, 0)) is computed for every rack but never asserted against r['facing'] or printed (only 5 sample racks are printed later in script 3).

strengths: Derives all rack placements, template selections, rotations, cold-aisle containment roofs and end doors, grid-aligned interior perforated tiles, and per-row cable trays directly from layout.json.

Automated recursive world-space bounding-box verification caught a subtle scene detail (unapplied 1.3333 X scale on the RackG root object), which was quickly diagnosed in script 2 and resolved to 0 mismatches in script 3.
Checks 2D AABB collisions across all rack pairs and against Wall_* and Column_* objects, and verifies world-space forward vectors across all four compass directions (N, S, E, W).

Efficient scene and workflow: uses linked duplicates for all 58 multi-part racks, reuses a single mesh datablock across all 34 perforated tiles, purges orphan meshes on rebuild, and finishes in just 3 scripts.
Y.summary: Strong, accurate implementation that fulfills all five deliverables from layout.json and uses effective automated bounding-box and collision checks to catch and fix an unapplied scale on the RackG template in three concise scripts; minor deductions in code quality for dead code (dup_tree), an unused forward-vector calculation in build.py, and patching build.py via string-replaced exec rather than editing it cleanly.

pairs.reason: Scores — X: spec_compliance=5, derives_from_inputs=5, self_verification=5, code_quality=4, efficiency=5; Y: spec_compliance=4, derives_from_inputs=4, self_verification=3, code_quality=2, efficiency=3. X completes the scene cleanly in 3 scripts with zero failures, uses linked-duplicate hierarchies, shared tile meshes, unit-scale box meshes, dedicated collections, and full orphan-mesh cleanup, and verifies recursive world-space mesh bounding boxes against expected dimensions and actual scene Wall_* and Column_* objects. Although Y adds boolean perforation holes to PerfTile_*, Y crashes in 4 of 9 scripts and leaves a stray boolean cutter object inside Cold Aisle 1 in the final scene. Bugs in X: (1) [medium, script 1] root.scale = (1, 1, 1) overwrote RackG's 1.3333 X root scale, shrinking 800 mm racks B01-B03 to 600 mm wide, caught immediately by X's world-bbox check and fixed in script 3; (2) [low, scripts 1 and 3] unused dead dup_tree helper and unused fwd vector in build.py, and fix.py patched via string-replace exec instead of updating build.py on disk. Bugs in Y: (1) [high, script 7] modifier_apply raised RuntimeError on multi-user mesh data before objects.remove(cutter) executed, leaving the 'hole' cutter object (25 cylinders at x=13.3..13.7, y=3.1..3.5, z=0.5..0.7) in scene.collection protruding 10 cm above the floor in Cold Aisle 1, missed by script 9's prefix-only check, plus orphan 'hole' meshes from scripts 2, 5, 7, and 8; (2) [medium, scripts 2 and 5] subtracting half-thickness after scaling centered cube verts shifted local Z to [-h, 0] while also offsetting location.z by -h/2, placing PerfTile_* top faces at z=0.58 and z=0.585 instead of 0.6 until script 8; (3) [medium, script 5] boolean cutter was built around world origin (0, 0, 0) while PerfTile_1_01 stood at (13.5, 3.3, 0.585), missing the tile completely and unsharing its mesh from the other 33 tiles; (4) [medium, scripts 1-3] script 1 crashed calling new.children.clear() (AttributeError), scripts 1-2 crashed indexing a[4] on a 4-tuple slice in overlap() (IndexError), and scripts 1-3 compared rack corners in metres against room['polygon'] in millimetres while script 3 also passed (x0, x1) instead of (x0, y0) as (x, y) and checked JSON data rather than scene Wall_*/Column_* objects; (5) [low, script 6] KeyError on 'PerfTile_3_10' due to global 01..34 numbering combined with aisle prefix.
